What it sets out to do02

Four aims, and what counts as achieved

AimMechanismEvidence it works
Validate, not rank Six agents gather evidence and try to falsify the claim Four verdicts; no compound is ever generated
Know when it cannot Six-dimension uncertainty vector, explicit abstain criteria 100% abstention on unknowns, 0 wrong pairs supported
Learn from real data GNN on measured assays; RL on the live tool environment MAE 0.662–0.860 across three datasets; return 0.85
Be checkable Calibration study, provenance manifest, 142 tests, two engines AUROC 1.00, Brier 0.068, every figure traceable

The output03

Four verdicts instead of one confidence score

SupportedEvidence agrees

Weighted support high, models consistent, uncertainty low.

ContradictedEvidence disagrees

Majority of pair-specific literature, or the assay, argues against.

UncertainEvidence is split

Something was found, but it does not settle the claim.

AbstainIt could not look

Coverage, assay or graph path missing — so it refuses.

src/core/verdict.py · thresholds in config.py03
Agentic AI04

Six agents, one of which argues against you

StepAgentWhat it does
01Planner Turns the claim into five checks that would settle it
02Evidence Literature, knowledge-graph paths, assay rows — each weighted
03Analysis QSAR, GNN embedding, and a real Vina pose when a structure exists
04Critic Finds disconfirming evidence and model disagreement
05Adaptive planner Widens the search or stops — capped at two retries
06Decision Reads the six dimensions and picks one of four verdicts
src/agents/*.py · shared state in src/core/state.py · LangGraph engine or an API-compatible shim04
Agentic AI05

How a hypothesis moves through the system

01–02Plan & gather Five checks, then literature + graph + assays
03Compute QSAR, GNN, docking — real pose if structured
04–05Falsify Critic looks for the counter-case; planner may loop back
06Decide Supported · contradicted · uncertain · abstain

Loop 05 → 02 runs at most twice; every agent appends to the audit trail the report carries

python main.py --drug SHP099 --target SHP2 → SUPPORTED, uncertainty 0.1205

Deep learning · model07

The GNN reads a molecule as a graph

01Atoms One-hot element, degree, aromatic and ring flags
02Two passes Degree-normalised neighbour aggregation, tanh
03Pooling Mean over atoms, dropout 0.15, one vector per molecule
04Head Scalar output — MSE for regression, BCE for classification

32-dim hidden state · Adam · 2 layers · trained by training/train_gnn.py with --resume

src/tools/gnn_torch.py — the same encoder feeds the binding readout07

What the agents add over a single model call

BehaviourHow it is implementedWhat it produced
Plans before it looks Planner writes five checks; evidence must satisfy them Abstain reasons that name the missing check
Looks again when thin Adaptive planner sets next_action and re-enters retrieval Wider search, capped at two loops
Argues against itself Critic is scored on disconfirming evidence, not agreement Contradicted verdicts on real data
Refuses to guess Explicit abstain criteria, never a prompt instruction 100% abstention on unknowns

The bug it caught

Brier 0.43 → 0.068

Any paper mentioning the target counted as support for any drug paired with it. Fixing that moved balanced accuracy 0.28 → 0.83.

evaluation/run_calibration.py · 6 true pairs, 12 wrong-target pairs, 2 unknowns13

Limits17

Where the prototype stops

Calibration20 internal cases

Drawn from the same seed corpus the agents read, so 0.83 is optimistic until an external benchmark runs.

Docking siteCatalytic, not allosteric

3O5X is the catalytic domain; SHP099 is allosteric. The pose is real, the binding mode is not. Register 5EHR for that.

Model scopeAssays, not affinity

The encoder learns chemistry from solubility and IC50 data; the affinity readout on top of it is rule-based.

Stated on the slide, not only in the README17
